title: Refine-to-plan file handoff to cut auto_plan token cost
problem: auto_plan currently tells Claude to 'explore the codebase freely' and on T3 it burned 564K tokens across 17 tool uses — mostly re-reading files that auto_refine had already examined. Each runner stage is a fresh subprocess, so there is no shared memory of 'which files have already been looked at' between refine and plan. This is a recurring cost driver across every ticket the runner runs.
description: Extend the spec schema produced by auto_refine with a files_examined field: a list of {path, sha, one_line_summary} entries for every file auto_refine actually read during refinement. auto_plan then trusts that list as its initial file-knowledge snapshot and is instructed in its prompt to (a) treat the listed files as already-read, (b) only re-read a file from the list if its spec-level behavior is about to change, and (c) keep its own exploration limited to files NOT on the list. validate_spec is updated to allow (but not require) the new field so existing specs remain valid. Backward compatible: if files_examined is absent or empty, auto_plan falls back to its current bounded exploration behavior (the one landed in this same session as fix #2a). Rough savings estimate: 30-50 percent off auto_plan on tickets where refine did real exploration, which is most of them.
scope: (1) Add optional files_examined field to the spec schema in validate_spec.py, with per-entry validation (path is a string, sha is optional hex, summary is a string). (2) Modify auto_refine.py to capture the set of files it read during refinement and emit them as files_examined in the spec output, including short summaries. (3) Modify auto_plan.py's prompt to consume the field and give the model explicit instructions about trusting it. (4) Add regression tests in runner/test_orchestrator.py or a new test file covering: spec with files_examined, spec without files_examined (backward compat), auto_plan actually reducing tool uses when files_examined is populated. (5) Run the full runner on a representative ticket and compare auto_plan token cost to T3's baseline (564K) as acceptance evidence. OUT OF SCOPE: changing auto_refine to use prompt caching, switching planner model tiers, or any executor-side changes — those are separate cost-reduction workstreams.
context: Discovered on 2026-04-06 during post-T3 cost investigation. Related to the (dropped) Sonnet-by-default idea and the (deferred) prompt-caching idea. T3 cost breakdown showed auto_plan at 22 percent of total runner cost, 2nd only to executor. Fix #2a (scoping the 'explore freely' prompt) landed in the same session but only treats the symptom; this ticket treats the root cause of duplicate file reads across stages.
